definitions.gloss: Go; the board game of Go
definitions.explanation: A strategic board game played with black and white stones on a 19×19 grid, where players compete to control territory. One of the oldest and most respected board games in East Asia.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎週|まいしゅう}→毎週：00730_maishuu⟧{囲碁|いご}⟦{教室|きょうしつ}→教室：00794_kyoushitsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{通|かよ}っている→通う：01217_kayou⟧。
examples.english: My grandfather goes to Go classes every week.

examples.japanese: {囲碁|いご}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{世界|せかい}→世界：01447_sekai⟧⟦{大会|たいかい}→大会：03386_taikai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{棋士|きし}→棋士：27809_kishi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{優勝|ゆうしょう}した→優勝する：25496_yuushousuru⟧。
examples.english: A Japanese Go player won the world championship.

notes:
{囲碁|いご} is the Japanese name for the board game Go, one of the oldest strategy games in the world. Often shortened to just ⟦{碁|ご}→碁：02138_go⟧ in casual speech.

KEY VOCABULARY:
- ⟦{碁盤|ごばん}→碁盤：13716_goban⟧: Go board
- ⟦{碁石|ごいし}→碁石：19754_goishi⟧: Go stones
- ⟦{対局|たいきょく}→対局：17420_taikyoku⟧: match, game
- ⟦{棋士|きし}→棋士：27809_kishi⟧: professional Go player
- ⟦{段|だん}→段：03424_dan⟧: rank (e.g., ⟦{初段|しょだん}→初段：28129_shodan⟧, {九段|くだん})
- ⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧: a move

USAGE:
The verb for playing Go is ⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧ (to play/strike), not ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: ⟦{碁|ご}→碁：02138_go⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧. This is shared with ⟦{将棋|しょうぎ}→将棋：04172_shougi⟧.

WATCH OUT:
Not to be confused with ⟦{以後|いご}→以後：01710_igo⟧ (from now on, hereafter) — same reading, different kanji and meaning.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Go has a long tradition in Japan. The {日本棋院|にほんきいん} (Nihon Ki-in) is the main professional organization.
